fields.name: Bulletin board
fields.label: Have you checked the Bulletin Board?
fields.help: Open the shift bulletin board and refresh the webpage.

fields.name: NOvA ECL
fields.label: Reviewed recent entries in the ECL?
fields.help: Review recent entries in the ECL .

fields.name: AD Elog
fields.label: Have you checked the AD E-log?
fields.help: The MCR shifter records your information in the AD E-log when you check in. Make sure that your information is correctly recorded: here . Please call them back if it is not correct or not visible after 30 minutes.

fields.name: Zoom
fields.label: Can you call into zoom?
fields.help: If not at a ROC , we don’t expect you to be called into zoom from your home for 8 hours. But please make sure you have the ability just in case. Join from PC, Mac, Linux, iOS or Android: https://fnal.zoom.us/j/93471617807 (the password can be found at docDB 55842 )

fields.name: Current RunCo
fields.label: Who is the current RunCo?
fields.help: Who is the current run coordinator? You can find that information on the shift bulletin board .

fields.name: Current DAQ expert
fields.label: Who is the current DAQ expert?
fields.help: See the shift bulletin board .

fields.name: Current DCS expert
fields.label: Who is the current DCS expert?
fields.help: See the shift bulletin board .

fields.name: Displays
fields.label: Are all display screens present?
fields.help: If not, see Shift Handbook for instructions for standard Control Room configuration.

fields.name: FD Runs in progress
fields.label: List the FD run in progress
fields.help: Go to the snapshot of FD-CR-01 . Check that the timestamp on the upper right is up-to-date. List the current FD run in progress. Use the format: Run #/Subrun #, e.g. 29127/34

fields.name: FD dashboard status
fields.label: Alarm/warning/ackeds in FD Dashboard
fields.help: List the number of entries in the ‘Alarm’, ‘Warning’ and ‘Acked’ columns for the FD DAQ Dashboard. This information will be useful later when the stable-running-checklist asks you if there are any new alarms or warnings in the DAQ Dashboard. Please use the following example to format your answer: Alarm: 0, Warning: 850 ( DAQ : 652, DCM : 197, Spill: 1), Acked: 0 The Alarm and Acked columns should be empty . If there is a persistent alarm in either dashboard you should contact the DAQ on-call expert straight away. Entries left in the Acked column can suppress further Warnings/Alarms in the same category, you should contact the DAQ on-call expert to clear anything that has been left as acknowledged in the dashboard.

fields.name: ND Runs in progress
fields.label: ND run in progress
fields.help: Go to the snapshot of ND-CR-01 . Check that the timestamp on the lower right is up-to-date. List the current ND run in progress. Use the format: Run #/Subrun #, e.g. 29127/34

fields.name: ND dashboard status
fields.label: Alarm/warning/ackeds in ND Dashboard
fields.help: List the number of entries in the ‘Alarm’, ‘Warning’ and ‘Acked’ columns, for the ND DAQ Dashboard. Please use the following example to format your answer: Alarm: 0, Warning: 53 ( DAQ : 49, DCM : 4), Acked: 0 Remember the Alarm and Acked columns should be empty . If there is a persistent alarm in either dashboard, contact the DAQ on-call expert now.

fields.name: Is NuMI beam running ?
fields.label: Is NuMI beam running ?
fields.help: For the next questions, check the middle left plot at: NuMI plots .

fields.name: NuMI beam intensity
fields.label: NuMI beam intensity
fields.help: Proton Intensity (E12).

fields.name: NuMI beam power
fields.label: NuMI beam power in kW
fields.help: Cycle Average Power.

fields.name: Is BNB running?
fields.label: Is BNB running?
fields.help: For the next questions, check the middle left plot at: BNB plots .

fields.name: BNB beam intensity
fields.label: BNB beam intensity
fields.help: Proton Intensity (E12).

fields.name: BNB beam power
fields.label: BNB beam power
fields.help: Protons Rate/hr.

fields.name: comments
fields.label: Comments
fields.help: Any comments on the state of things as you found them at the start of your shift? Plans for this shift?

fields.name: typical_power
fields.label: What is the typical power while beam is up?
fields.help: Go to the NuMI status page . From the beam intensity/average power plot estimate the current average power if the beam is up or recently dropped out (<10 minutes). If there has been no beam for more than 10 minutes, put “N/A”.

fields.name: fd_run_number
fields.label: FarDet run and subrun
fields.help: You can find both of these listed in run control on FarDet VNC -01. Please enter them in the format: Run #/Subrun #. If the run is stopped for an understood reason , please enter N/A instead.

fields.name: fd_dashboard_running
fields.label: FD Dashboard running and up to date?
fields.help: The Dashboard should be clearly visible on FarDet CR-01. If the dashboard is not running contact your DAQ on-call expert . There is a timestamp in the top-right corner of the GUI . If this timestamp is out of date by more than 5 mins, contact your DAQ on-call expert . The ‘Last Update’ timestamp below it is when the last new alarm/message comes in, so it is ok if this one is out of date.

fields.name: fd_dashboard_alarms
choices: Yes - new alarms in the Dashboard - calling expert
Yes - new warnings in the Dashboard
fields.label: Any new alarms or warnings in the Dashboard?
fields.help: Check the following: If there are any red boxes at the top, contact your DAQ on-call expert to address the issue. If there are any yellow boxes, email your DAQ on-call expert and CC nova_runcoordinator@fnal.gov. Check the alarm column. If there are new entries contact your DAQ on-call expert . Check the warning column. No action required for new warnings, but pay attention to large bursts of warnings which could indicate a more serious problem.

fields.name: fd_rack_temps
choices: No; out of date: contacting DAQ on-call and RunCo
No; network problems: contacting DAQ on-call & RunCo
No; temperature(s) >90F: contacting DAQ on-call & RunCo
fields.label: Are the FarDet rack temperatures OK?
fields.help: You should check the following: Check the “Last updated at:” timestamp. If this is out of date by more than 5 mins, go to see the rack temperatures at the bottom right of the FD- VNC -01 to see if it is updating. If the timestamp is still out of date contact your DAQ on-call expert and run coordinator. If the GUI is flashing red and blue and warns of a connection problem, contact your DAQ on-call expert and run coordinator. The GUI will also flash red and blue, If any temperature rises above 90 F. If this happens contact your run coordinator and DAQ on-call expert . If all temperatures are OK, but any are above 85 F you should continue to closely monitor their values until the temperature(s) begin to fall.

fields.name: fd_numi_rate
fields.label: Average rate for the FarDet NuMI spill
fields.help: This should be between about 0.4-1.0 Hz, depending on beam power/intensity.

fields.name: fd_cosmic_rate
fields.label: Average rate for the FarDet Cosmic spill
fields.help: The nominal rate for cosmics is 3.33 Hz.

fields.name: fd_one_hz_rate
fields.label: Average rate for the FarDet 1Hz trigger
fields.help: The nominal rate is 1 Hz.

fields.name: fd_ddt_total_rate
fields.label: Average rate for DDT: Total trigger
fields.help: The acceptable rate for DDT total can change drastically depending on which DDT s are running/firing. You should just check the rate is between 60 and 100 Hz and the number of triggers in the total is advancing. If the rate is outside of that range, please contact your DAQ expert .

fields.name: fd_event_display_updating
choices: No: calling expert because it is not running/frozen/out-of-date
No: run stopped for expert activity
fields.label: FD event display visible and updating?
fields.help: The event display should be present at the top-left of FarDet VNC -02. If the event display needs to be started, contact your on-call DAQ expert Check the timestamp of the last event (in the bottom-left corner of the display) is not more than 5 mins out of date, and at the top of the GUI check the event display is set to auto advance (there should be a X to the right of the Next -----> button. Next go to the NOvA live event display website if the FD event display is not updating every 5 seconds contact your DAQ expert.

fields.name: fd_event_display_ok
choices: No: broken tracks or missing DCMs - calling expert
No: run stopped for expert activity
fields.label: Does the event display look OK?
fields.help: Watch the NOvA live event display website for a few events and check that: You don’t see broken tracks All DCM s have hits in them sometimes

fields.name: fd_onmon_updating
choices: Contacting expert because it is frozen or out of date
No: run stopped for expert activity
fields.label: FarDet OnMon visible and updating?
fields.help: The OnMon GUI should be present at the bottom-left of FarDet VNC -02. There should be two OnMon GUI s present. The FEBHitRateMap should be shown at the bottom-left of FarDet VNC -02, and AEVsHour should be above that. If either GUI is not running contact your on-call DAQ expert . You can tell if it is updating by checking the timestamp (see the next question).

fields.name: fd_onmom_timestamp
choices: older than 5 mins - calling DAQ expert
fields.label: What is the value of the OnMon timestamp?
fields.help: Check the timestamp in the top-right corner of the GUI s, enter the value here, and make sure it is NOT more than 5 mins ago (note the timestamp is in UTC ). If either OnMon is frozen or not updating contact your DAQ expert to kill and restart it. The reason for this question is to make sure we have OnMon updating, since sometimes it stops. We used to see the OnMon frozen for 1.5 days without noticing it during checklist shifts, which can be dangerous.

fields.name: fd_feb_hit_rate
choices: No: sections with high/low rate - calling expert
No: run stopped for expert activity
fields.label: Does the FEBHitRateMap look OK?
fields.help: Go to the FEBHitRateMap plot . Are there any DCM s with no hits? Do the rates look OK? Most FEB s should show a green-yellow colour. If there are DCM s or large portions of the detector showing a rate that is much higher or lower than the rest of the detector, this could indicate a serious problem. Check the time that the plot was last updated, this plot should update every 20 minutes. A timestamp older than this could indicate that the web-plot making scripts aren’t running.

fields.name: fd_incomplete_events
choices: Yes - contacting the DAQ on-call expert
fields.label: Continuous incomplete events for >20 mins?
fields.help: Look at the OnMon view displaying the “Number of errors per minute as a function of UTC hour”. If there is an entry under “Incomplete Events” for more than 20 consecutive minutes (each bin is 1 minute), contact your DAQ on-call expert and attach a screenshot of the plot to this form.

fields.name: fd_css_updating
choices: No- contacting an expert to start it
fields.label: FarDet CSS GUI updating?
fields.help: The CSS GUI should be visible in the top-right corner of FarDet VNC -02, showing the “FarDet Overview” page. If you need to start the GUI contact your DAQ on-call expert . If the GUI is updating the heartbeat circle will change color every time the snapshot server updates. Please watch the snapshot image for a minute to ensure the color is changing. If is is not the GUI may be frozen or not updating. Please contact the expert on-call.

fields.name: fd_detector_cooled
choices: No: one or more DCMs warm (dark green): calling expert
No: DCMs red or other non-green state: calling expert
fields.label: Is the FarDet cooled?
fields.help: All DCM s should show a light green color if the detector is cooled. If one or more DCM s are consistently in the alarm (red) state, or any other (non-green) state, you should contact the expert on-call .

fields.name: nd_run_number
fields.label: NearDet run and subrun
fields.help: You can find both of these listed in run control on NearDet VNC -01. Please enter them in the format: Run #/Subrun # If the run is stopped for an understood reason , please enter N/A instead.

fields.name: nd_dashboard_running
choices: Contacting the expert because it is frozen or out of date
No: contacting the expert to start it
No: run stopped for expert activity
fields.label: ND Dashboard running, timestamp < 20 mins ago?
fields.help: The Dashboard should be visible on NearDet VNC -01. If it is not running contact your DAQ on-call expert . There is a timestamp in the top-right corner of the GUI . If this timestamp is out of date by more than 5 mins you should contact your DAQ on-call expert address this issue. The ‘Last Update’ timestamp below it is when the last new alarm/message comes in, so it is ok if this one is out of date.

fields.name: nd_dashboard_alarms
choices: Yes - new alarms in the Dashboard - calling expert
Yes - new warnings in the Dashboard
fields.label: Any new alarms or warnings in the Dashboard?
fields.help: Check the following: If any boxes are red, call your DAQ on-call expert . If any boxes are yellow, email your DAQ on-call expert and CC nova_runcoordinator@fnal.gov. Check the alarm column. If there are new entries call your DAQ on-call expert . Check the warning column. No action required for new warnings, but pay attention to large bursts of warnings which could indicate a more serious problem.

fields.name: nd_numi_rate
fields.label: Average rate for NearDet NuMI spill
fields.help: This should be between about 0.4-0.8 Hz, depending on beam power/intensity.

fields.name: nd_booster_rate
fields.label: Average rate for NearDet Booster spill
fields.help: This should be between about 4-6 Hz, depending on beam power/intensity. If the BNB beam is down you can enter N/A.

fields.name: nd_one_hz_rate
fields.label: Average rate for the NearDet 1Hz trigger
fields.help: The nominal rate is 1 Hz.

fields.name: nd_cosmic_rate
fields.label: Average rate for the NearDet Cosmic spill
fields.help: The nominal rate for cosmics is 1 Hz.

fields.name: nd_ddt_total_rate
fields.label: Average rate for DDT: Total trigger
fields.help: You should just check the rate is between 25 and 40 Hz and the number of triggers in the total is advancing. If the rate is outside of that range, please contact your DAQ expert .

fields.name: nd_numi_event_display
choices: No: contacting expert because it is frozen or out of date
No: but there is no beam
No: run stopped for expert activity
fields.label: ND NuMI event display updating?
fields.help: The event display should be present at the top-left of NearDet VNC -02 (upper plot). If the event display needs to be started, contact your on-call DAQ expert. The event display will not update if there are no new events, so if the beam is down the display may look like it is not updating/frozen until beam returns. If beam is down you do not need to call a DAQ expert. Instead check the AD Elog or call the MCR for details. Check the timestamp of the last event (in the bottom-left corner of the display) is not more than 5 mins out of date, and at the top of the GUI check the event display is set to auto advance (there should be a X to the right of the Next ——-> button. Next go to the NOvA live event displays website . If the ND NuMI event display is not updating every 5 seconds contact your DAQ expert.

fields.name: nd_numi_event_display_ok
choices: No - but there is no beam
fields.label: Does the NuMI event display look OK?
fields.help: Watch the event display for a few events and check that: You don’t see broken tracks All DCM s sometimes have hits in them

fields.name: nd_all_triggers_event_display_updating
choices: Contacting expert because it is frozen or out of date
fields.label: ND all-triggers event display updating?
fields.help: The event display should be present at the top-left of NearDet VNC -02 (lower plot). If the event display needs to be started, contact your on-call DAQ expert . Check the timestamp of the last event (in the bottom-left corner of the display) is not more than 5 mins out of date, and at the top of the GUI check the event display is set to auto advance (there should be a X to the right of the Next ——-> button. Next go to the NOvA live event displays website . If the ND all triggers event display is not updating every 5 seconds contact your DAQ expert .

fields.name: nd_all_triggers_event_display_ok
fields.label: Does the all triggers event display look OK?
fields.help: Watch the event display for a few events and check that: You don’t see broken tracks You don’t consistently see no hits in a DCM

fields.name: nd_onmon_updating
choices: No: Contacting expert because it is frozen or out of date
No: contacting an expert to start it now
No: run stopped for expert activity
fields.label: NearDet OnMon visible and updating?
fields.help: There should be two OnMon GUI s present. The FEBHitRateMap should be shown at the bottom-left of NearDet VNC -02, and AEVsHour should be to the right of that. If either GUI is not running contact your on-call DAQ expert . You can tell if it is updating by checking the timestamp (see the next question).

fields.name: nd_onmon_timestamp
choices: older than 5 mins - calling DAQ expert
fields.label: What is the value of the OnMon timestamp?
fields.help: Check the timestamp in the top-right corner of the GUI s (note the timestamp is in UTC ). If either OnMon is frozen or not updating contact your DAQ expert to restart it.

fields.name: nd_feb_hit_rate
fields.label: Does the FEBHitRateMap look OK?
fields.help: Please check the event displays at the FEBHitRateMap plot . Are there any DCM s with no hits? Do the rates look OK? Most FEB s should show a green-yellow colour. If there are DCM s or large portions of the detector showing a rate that is much higher or lower than the rest of the detector, this could indicate a serious problem. Check the time that the plot was last updated, this plot should update every 20 minutes. A timestamp older than this could indicate that the web-plot making scripts aren’t running.

fields.name: nd_timing_peak
fields.label: ND timing peak visible and between the lines?
fields.help: Go to the TimingALLVsHour plot . Check the ND timing peak observable (cyan/green color) and it is in between the dotted white lines?

fields.name: nd_incomplete_events
choices: Yes - contacting the DAQ on-call expert
fields.label: Continuous incomplete events for >20 mins?
fields.help: Look at the OnMon view displaying the “Number of errors per minute as a function of UTC hour”. If there is an entry under “Incomplete Events” for more than 20 consecutive minutes (each bin is 1 minute), contact your DAQ on-call expert and attach a screenshot of the plot to this form.

fields.name: nd_css_updating
choices: No: Contacting expert because it is frozen or out of date
No: Contacting expert to start it
fields.label: NearDet CSS GUI updating?
fields.help: The CSS GUI should be visible in the top-right corner of NearDet VNC -02, showing the “NearDet Overview” page. If it needs to be started, contact your DAQ on-call expert . If the GUI is updating the heartbeat circle will change color every time the snapshot server updates. Please watch the snapshot image for a minute to ensure the color is changing. If the color is not changing it could indicate it is frozen or not updating. If the GUI is frozen or not updating contact a DCS expert listed on the Blue Expert Sheet.

fields.name: nd_detector_cooled
choices: No - one or more DCMs warm (dark green)
No - DCMs red or other non-green state
fields.label: Is the NearDet cooled?
fields.help: All DCM s should show a light green color if the detector is cooled. If one or more DCM s are consistently in the alarm (red) state, or any other (non-green) state, contact the on-call expert .

fields.name: nearline_open
choices: One or more plots are out of date
One or more plots are largely blank
fields.label: Nearline front page visible and up to date?
fields.help: You should check the “Last updated on:” timestamp is no older than 20 mins. A timestamp older than this could indicate that the web-plot making scripts aren’t running. The plots are populated from the right as sub-runs finish, so for the near detector, it may take up to 1.5 hours for new data to appear. However, if a large section of the plot is blank and the detector is up with a run going, then this is an indication that the nearline processing has stopped. If either of these is true you should contact a Nearline Software expert .

fields.name: fd_nearline_features
fields.label: What features are visible in the FD plots?

fields.name: nd_nearline_features
fields.label: What features are visible in the ND plots?

fields.name: nearline_details
fields.label: Provide additional details
fields.help: Use this box to describe, for both detectors: The features in more detail. Any action taken. Use the notation: ( NOT ) RESOLVED – description of feature including times – action taken . e.g. RESOLVED – FEB Hit rate drop – 14:00 to 15:30 – DCM sync issues identified for that period. NOT RESOLVED – Gap – 20:00 to 23:00 – contacted expert. Think about the features you see in the context of current running conditions, beam/detector downtimes, etc. Are they consistent? If there are features you do not understand follow the wiki links on the Nearline front page learn more about interpreting these plots and when you should contact an expert.

fields.name: vnc_02s_attached
fields.label: Near and Far VNC-02 images attached?

fields.name: additional_info
fields.label: Additional information
fields.help: Use this box to provide further information on your interpretation of the event displays, OnMon plots and Nearline front page plots. You can attach additional plots/screenshot to refer to.

fields.name: cr01_time
choices: Older than 5 mins: calling DAQ expert
fields.label: Last update time of FD-01 desktop?
fields.help: Make sure the timestamp in lower-right corner is up to date (no older than 5 mins).

fields.name: cr01_windows_present
choices: No: calling the DAQ expert now
No: run stopped for expert work
fields.label: Are all FD-01 windows present?
fields.help: If not at a ROC , go to the snapshot of FD- VNC -01 . Are all windows present that should be? If something is missing, there will be a blank space on the background with text that says “ X should be here.” Please call the DAQ expert.

fields.name: cr01_rack_temps
choices: No: calling DAQ expert & RunCo now
fields.label: Rack Temps OK?
fields.help: Check that the monitoring page is up to date and is not in alarm. If there are any alarms, call the DAQ expert and the run coordinator immediately. You can also see the rack temperatures at the bottom right of the FD- VNC -01 in your own browser.

fields.name: cr01_tcr_page_ok
choices: No: calling the DAQ expert now
fields.label: TCR page okay?
fields.help: Check that the timing status page is visible towards the bottom right and that the status is “Running” and “Synchronized”. If not, call the timing expert.

fields.name: cr01_spill_server_green
choices: No: but there is ongoing expert work
fields.label: Spill Server GUI green?
fields.help: Are all boxes in the Spill server GUI green? If not, call the DAQ expert.

fields.name: cr02_time
choices: Older than 5 mins: calling DAQ expert
fields.label: Last update time of FD-02 desktop?
fields.help: Make sure the timestamp in the lower-right corner is up to date (no older than 5 mins).

fields.name: cr02_windows_present
choices: No: run stopped for expert work
fields.label: Are all FD-VNC-02 windows present?
fields.help: If not at a ROC , go to the snapshot of FD- VNC -02 . Check that the timestamp on the lower right is up-to-date. Are all windows present that should be? If not, call the expert. On this screen there should be the Far Detector: Event Display, CSS GUI , two copies of OnMon, the DiskWatcher terminal, and a webpage showing four Nearline plots.

fields.name: cr02_diskwatcher_heartbeat
fields.label: DiskWatcher Heartbeat
fields.help: What is the time stamp from the last disk-watcher heartbeat in the console in the center right? If this time stamp is more than 2 hours old, call the DAQ expert.

fields.name: cr02_loadshed_check
choices: More than 5 mins: calling DAQ expert
fields.label: Loadshed Check
fields.help: In the most recent LoadshedCheck message in the DiskWatcher terminal window, how many seconds has it been since the Loadshed last updated? The Loadshed should update once every five minutes, so if this number is more than 300 seconds, contact the DAQ on-call and inform them the Loadshed is not updating.

fields.name: cr03_time
choices: Older than 5 mins  - calling DAQ expert
fields.label: Last update time of synoptic desktop?
fields.help: Make sure the timestamp in the lower-right corner is up to date (no older than 5 mins).

fields.name: cr03_windows_present
choices: No: run stopped for expert work
fields.label: Are all synoptic windows present?
fields.help: If not at a ROC , go to the snapshot of synoptic displays . Check that the timestamp on the lower right is up-to-date. Are all windows present that should be? On this screen there should be 10 GUI s.

fields.name: cr03_timestamps
fields.label: Time stamps okay?
fields.help: Are the time stamps in the upper right corner of all 10 GUI windows present and up to date?

fields.name: cr03_all_green
choices: No: but there is ongoing expert work
fields.label: All boxes green?
fields.help: Short interrupts (< 30 seconds) can happen, so if you see purple or red boxes in a snapshot, refresh the to see if it goes away.

fields.name: cr03_dewpoint_nd
fields.label: Are all dew points under threshold (13 C) for ND ?
fields.help: Look at the upper left window (NOvA Near Detector Rack and Environmental Details). Are all the boxes labeled “DP” under 13 C? If not, call the DCS expert listed in the blue sheet.

fields.name: cr03_dewpoint_fd
fields.label: Are all dew points under threshold (55 F)  for FD?
fields.help: Look at the bottom left window (NOvA Far Detector Environmental Details). Are all the boxes under the “Dew point” column under 55 F ? If not, call the DCS expert listed in the blue sheet.

fields.name: cr04_cameras_updating
fields.label: Are the cameras updating?
fields.help: Go to the FD camera web page and the ND camera web page . If they are not visible or not, please note it in the log (here and in the shift summary), but do not wake up DAQ experts. Note that the web pages in the screenshots only reload every hour, so please use the links above.

fields.name: cr05_time
choices: Older than 5 mins: calling DAQ expert
fields.label: Last update time of ND-01 desktop?
fields.help: Make sure the timestamp in the lower-right corner is up to date (no older than 5 mins).

fields.name: cr05_windows_present
choices: No: run stopped for expert work
fields.label: Are all ND-01 windows present?
fields.help: Go to the snapshot of ND- VNC -01 . Check that the timestamp on the lower right is up-to-date. Are all windows present that should be? On this screen there should be 8 GUI s and 1 webpage.

fields.name: cr05_tcr_page_ok
choices: No: calling the timing expert now
No – experts aware so no action taken
fields.label: TCR page okay?
fields.help: Check that the timing status page is visible in the bottom right corner and that the status is “Running” and “Synchronized”. If not, call the timing expert.

fields.name: sn_gui_ok
choices: No: experts aware so no action taken
fields.label: Pre-supernova GUI okay?
fields.help: If it is showing purple, orange or red, follow the instructions in the window.

fields.name: cr05_spill_server_all_green
choices: No: but there is ongoing expert work
fields.label: Spill server all green?
fields.help: Are all boxes in the Spill server GUI green? If not, call the DAQ expert.

fields.name: cr06_time
choices: Older than 5 mins: calling DAQ expert
fields.label: Last update time of ND-02 desktop?
fields.help: Make sure the timestamp in the lower-right corner is up to date (no older than 5 mins).

fields.name: cr06_windows _present
choices: No: run stopped for expert work
fields.label: Are all ND-02 windows present?
fields.help: Go to the snapshot of ND- VNC -02 . Check that the timestamp on the lower right is up-to-date. Are all windows present that should be? On this screen there should be 4 GUI s, 1 terminal, and 1 webpage. During beam shutdown, the beam event display is disabled, so there will be one fewer GUI and terminal.

fields.name: cr06_diskwatcher_heartbeat
choices: Older than 25 mins: calling DAQ expert
fields.label: Disk watcher heartbeat
fields.help: What is the time stamp from the last disk-watcher heartbeat in the console on the center right? If this time stamp is more than 25 minutes old, call the DAQ expert.

fields.name: screenshots
fields.label: Attach screenshots
fields.help: Please add screenshots of all 6 desktops.

fields.name: additional_info
fields.label: Additional information
fields.help: Use this for general comments and to provide further details of anything you found that may suggest a problem.

fields.name: Shadow Shifter Name
fields.label: Shadow Shifter Name
fields.help: If no shadow shifter, leave blank. A guide to shadow shifting can be found here.

fields.name: Call MCR
fields.label: Call MCR
fields.help: Call MCR at +1 (630) 840-3721 and identify yourself as the NOvA shifter. Give them your name, contact number of your ROC or institution, and the name of your institution. If you are calling from a ROC , please let them know that.

fields.name: Zoom
choices: No: but I'm doing it right now
fields.label: Have you met with the previous shifter on Zoom?
fields.help: Meet with previous shifter on Zoom to learn anything important that happened during their shift and the current status of the detectors. Join from PC, Mac, Linux, iOS or Android: https://fnal.zoom.us/j/93471617807 (the password can be found at docDB 48803 )

fields.name: City of current location
fields.label: City of current location?
fields.help: Give city of current location. Do not include your address.

fields.name: Equipment for shift
fields.label: Describe the equipment being used for your shift?
fields.help: If you are at a ROC , give the name of your ROC . Otherwise, give outline of equipment used (version numbers not needed). Example: mac laptop and chrome.

fields.name: General comments
fields.label: General comments
fields.help: Any general comments?

fields.name: Problem
fields.label: What is the problem?
fields.help: Include ECL entry numbers if appropriate. Attach a screenshot showing the problem, if possible.

fields.name: Expert
fields.label: Who is the expert being contacted?

fields.name: Type of contact
fields.label: How are you trying to contact them?

fields.name: Response
choices: Yes: they told me to contact someone else
No -- I left them information (text or voicemail)
No -- I didn't leave them information
fields.label: Did you get in contact?

fields.name: FD DAQ downtime
choices: Yes; but it will be resolved within 30 mins
Yes; FD may be down for >30 minutes - calling RunCo
fields.label: Is this a FD problem during NuMI running?
fields.help: If the Far Detector is expected to be down for more than 30 minutes, and NuMI beam is running, call the RunCo . Their contact information is on the Bulletin Board .

fields.name: Next Shifter
fields.label: Next Shifter
fields.help: Is the next shifter present? If not and it is 30 minutes past the start of the next shift, please call the run coordinator.

fields.name: Info Transfer
fields.label: Info Transfer
fields.help: Have you informed the next shifter of the current running conditions and/or any known issue that occurred during your shift?

fields.name: Shift summary
fields.label: Shift summary
fields.help: List any major incidents that occurred during your shift (crashes, DAQ work, ongoing issues, etc.)

fields.name: FD run summary
fields.label: FD run summary
fields.help: List the FD runs that completed during your shift. Please point out if any of these runs should be excluded from good data. For example, if the detector was running warm, or if it was being run with some kind of test configuration. Most data that is truly bad will be marked as such by our data quality criteria. But in the case of known bad runs (runs taking for testing purposes for example) it is better to make sure they are still marked as bad.

fields.name: ND run summary
fields.label: ND run summary
fields.help: List the ND runs that completed during your shift, with the same detail as for the FD.

fields.name: Fraction of good beam
fields.label: Fraction of good beam
fields.help: Go to Good Beam Fraction plot . Record the average fraction of good beam over the last 24 hours (the number in the top right corner.) This number should be above 0.7 and ensures that our spills are passing our beam quality cuts. If it is below 0.7 for multiple subruns, and beam has been running normally, please e-mail nova_runcoordinator@fnal.gov and nova_dataquality@fnal.gov. During beam shutdown, please enter N/A instead.

fields.name: Bad spills
fields.label: Bad spills
fields.help: Go to the Bad Spills plot This plot shows only the “bad” spills over the past 24 hours (keep in mind that there are ~66,000 spills during this time.) List the category from the horizontal axis with the most entries (obviously skipping “total bad spills”). If this category is anything other than “ POT ”, and there have been no known non-standard beam conditions that would cause a different failure (such as target scans) e-mail nova_runcoordinator@fnal.gov and nova_dataquality@fnal.gov. During beam shutdown, please enter N/A instead.

fields.name: Nearline plots
fields.label: Nearline plots
fields.help: Please attach all 8 plots (4 for each detector) from the nearline front-page, and check that each plot is up to date.

fields.name: Comments
fields.label: Comments
fields.help: Any further comments or comments about features in the nearline plots?

fields.name: MuonMonitorTime
choices: No - but there is no beam
fields.label: Muon monitor plots up to date?
fields.help: Check the last refreshed time stamp reported for each plot. If this time stamp occurred within the last 8 hours, the plots are considered up to date. If the plots are not up to date please email nova_runcoordinator@fnal.gov and mm_expert@listserv.fnal.gov

fields.name: MuonMonitorStatus
fields.label: What is their status?
fields.help: All plots are labeled with the status of the data as “Status: Good” or “Status: Not Good”, by checking if the data goes beyond the boundary drawn on the plots. Check that status of each plot. If any plot status is bad please email nova_runcoordinator@fnal.gov and mm_expert@listserv.fnal.gov

fields.name: MuonMonitorComment
fields.label: Comments
fields.help: Any comments about the features in the muon monitor plots? Are there any gaps or features not associated with beam down time or the recovery of the beam? If there are please email nova_runcoordinator@fnal.gov and mm_expert@listserv.fnal.gov
